position: Mission Statement for a Reformed Department of Energy
proposal: The Mandate recommends renaming DOE the Department of Energy Security and Advanced Science and refocusing it on five missions: energy security, promoting US energy interests abroad, advanced science, cleanup of weapons sites, and nuclear weapons and naval reactors. It proposes an Under Secretary for Energy Security overseeing CESER, Electricity, Nuclear Energy, Fossil Energy, EERE and the Strategic Petroleum Reserve.

status_summary: DOE has not been renamed: its organization chart dated 2025-11-20 and the department's chart page updated 2026-08-03 still carry the Department of Energy name, with an Under Secretary of Energy, Under Secretary for Science and Under Secretary for Nuclear Security and no Under Secretary for Energy Security. The 2025-11-20 reorganization renamed or created offices including Critical Minerals and Energy Innovation, Hydrocarbons and Geothermal Energy and Energy Dominance Financing, and the FY2027 Budget in Brief (April 2026) uses those names and a budget line for the Under Secretary for Energy. On 2026-03-17 the Office of Science announced a realignment of its own structure; AIP reported that the accompanying chart merged High Energy Physics and Nuclear Physics, but the Office of Science chart dated 2026-10-01 still lists them as separate offices, with one official heading the first and acting head of the second. On 2026-06-29 the House passed H.R. 7258, which would add energy emergency and security functions to those assigned to assistant secretaries; it was referred to a Senate committee on 2026-07-13 and is not a rename. No bill renaming the department was found.

timeline.event: DOE published an organization chart in which the Under Secretary for Infrastructure became the Under Secretary of Energy, the science under secretary was renamed, and new or renamed offices appear; the department name is unchanged.
The DOE Office of Science issued a bulletin announcing a realignment of its organizational structure, stating that the realignment had begun and would take a few months to take effect.
timeline.source: U.S. Department of Energy, Office of Science

timeline.event: The House passed H.R. 7258, the Energy Emergency Leadership Act of 2026, by voice vote; it amends the DOE Organization Act to add energy emergency and energy security functions to those assigned to assistant secretaries. It does not rename the department.
H.R. 7258 was received in the Senate and referred to the Energy and Natural Resources Committee.

title: Rename and restructure DOE as a Department of Energy Security and Advanced Science
uncertainties: The chart text lacks full reporting lines, so placement of offices relies on trade press (ANS, Latitude Media, Holland and Knight); the office names themselves, including the Office of Critical Minerals and Energy Innovation, the Hydrocarbons and Geothermal Energy Office and the Office of Energy Dominance Financing, appear on the chart and no Under Secretary for Energy Security appears there. No renaming bill was found in searches of AIP's science bill tracker and govinfo bill status pages, but congress.gov could not be searched directly. The 2026-08-03 date is the update line on the DOE chart page, and the dated chart file behind it was not located. The Office of Science bulletin of 2026-03-17 was opened; its text does not name the offices affected and shows the new structure only as an embedded image, so the merger of High Energy Physics and Nuclear Physics and the consolidation of operations offices rest on AIP's reading of that image. The Office of Science chart dated 2026-10-01 still shows High Energy Physics, Nuclear Physics, Sponsored Activities and the international and research security office as separate units, so whether the announced realignment has taken effect is unclear. FY2026 Energy and Water appropriations (Public Law 119-74) did not rename the department, per CRS. The FY2027 Budget in Brief was read through a summarizing fetch; it is a budget request document dated only to the month (April 2026) and is used as a source for office names rather than as a timeline event. Federal Register searches for DOE reorganization notices after 2025-11-20 returned only unrelated rules.
